\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The problem}

Tarski's theorem on the undefinability of truth is often summarized as an interdiction: a language may not contain its own truth predicate. The interdiction is real, but coarse. It concerns \emph{one particular} self-referential construction --- the diagonal one producing the liar --- and says nothing about the enormous space of self-referential constructions that are not diagonal.

The engineering counterpart of this coarseness is familiar. Recursive definitions in programming languages, inductive predicates in proof systems, recursive rules in deductive databases, and reflection principles in verified reasoning systems all involve a language defining objects of its own kind. All of them work. What distinguishes them from the liar is not the absence of self-reference but the presence of \emph{structure} --- monotonicity, stratification, or well-foundedness --- making a system of self-referential equations solvable.

This paper isolates that structure in the simplest setting where the phenomenon lives: propositional logic with a family of internal truth atoms. The setting is deliberately minimal --- no quantifiers, no arithmetization --- so that the mechanism is visible without the machinery of self-reference obscuring it. Every self-referential configuration is available by fiat: we simply \emph{stipulate} that the name $c$ denotes a formula mentioning $Tc$.

\subsection{The tangled-hierarchy thesis, formalized}

A \emph{tangled hierarchy}, in Hofstadter's sense, is a system of levels in which the top level reaches back down to the bottom; the accompanying claim is that the strange loop does not corrupt the levels it sits above. Read as mathematics, ``does not corrupt the levels above'' is exactly the technical notion of a \emph{conservative extension}: the theory of the tangled system entails no sentence of the old vocabulary that the old theory did not already entail. The results below give that claim a precise form, precise sufficient conditions, and a precise boundary. The conditions are generous; the boundary is the liar.

\subsection{Contributions}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Exact criterion} (Theorem~\ref{thm:char}): conservativity over all truth-free base theories is equivalent to expandability of every base valuation to a model of the loop equations.
\item \textbf{Positivity suffices} (Theorem~\ref{thm:pos}), via Knaster--Tarski, with no constraint on the reference graph.
\item \textbf{Groundedness yields determinacy} (Theorems~\ref{thm:groundeduniq}--\ref{thm:groundedcons}), for arbitrary polarity.
\item \textbf{Local stratification} (Theorem~\ref{thm:locstrat}): negative edges descend, positive edges stay put; strictly generalizes the previous two (Propositions~\ref{prop:strict}, \ref{prop:nonnec}).
\item \textbf{Height collapse} (Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse}): well-foundedness is equivalent to an $\mathbb{N}$-rank.
\item \textbf{Exact cost accounting} (Theorems~\ref{thm:determinacy}, \ref{thm:loops}, \ref{thm:trich}).
\item \textbf{Sharpness} (Theorem~\ref{thm:liar}): the liar destroys conservativity by inconsistency.
\end{enumerate}

\section{The language}

\subsection{Syntax}

Fix a set $A$ of \emph{atoms} (the vocabulary of the base, or ``old'', theory) and a set $I$ of \emph{names}.

\begin{definition}[Formulas]
The set $\Frm(A,I)$ is generated inductively by: $a$ for $a \in A$; $\bot$; $\varphi \to \psi$; and $Tc$ for $c \in I$ (the \emph{truth atom} of $c$).
\end{definition}

We abbreviate $\neg\varphi := \varphi \to \bot$ and
\[
  \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi \;:=\; \neg\big( (\varphi \to \psi) \to \neg(\psi \to \varphi) \big),
\]
which under the semantics below has exactly the truth table of the biconditional. Only $\bot$ and $\to$ are primitive.

\begin{definition}[Truth-free formulas]
A formula is \emph{truth-free} if it contains no truth atom: atoms and $\bot$ are truth-free, $\varphi \to \psi$ is truth-free iff both parts are, and $Tc$ is never truth-free. The truth-free formulas constitute the \emph{old language}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Occurrence]
The name $c$ \emph{occurs} in $\varphi$, written $\Occ(c,\varphi)$, if $\varphi = Tc$, or $\varphi = \varphi_1 \to \varphi_2$ and $c$ occurs in $\varphi_1$ or $\varphi_2$. No name occurs in an atom or in $\bot$.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Polarity}

\begin{definition}[Global polarity]
Define $\Pol(b,\varphi)$ for $b \in \{+,-\}$ by recursion: $\Pol(b,a)$ and $\Pol(b,\bot)$ hold for both signs; $\Pol(b, \varphi \to \psi)$ iff $\Pol(\bar b, \varphi)$ and $\Pol(b,\psi)$; $\Pol(b, Tc)$ iff $b = +$. A formula is \emph{positive} if $\Pol(+,\varphi)$ and \emph{negative} if $\Pol(-,\varphi)$; equivalently, $\varphi$ is negative iff $\neg\varphi$ is positive. Every truth-free formula is both, and no truth atom is negative.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polarized occurrence]
$\Occ^{b}(c,\varphi)$ for $b \in \{+,-\}$: neither sign holds at atoms or $\bot$; $\Occ^{b}(c, \varphi\to\psi)$ iff $\Occ^{\bar b}(c,\varphi)$ or $\Occ^{b}(c,\psi)$; $\Occ^{b}(c, Tc')$ iff $b=+$ and $c'=c$. Thus $c$ occurs positively (negatively) if some occurrence of $Tc$ lies under an even (odd) number of antecedent positions. A name may occur both ways: in $Tc \to Tc$ it does.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:polocc}
(i) $\Occ^{b}(c,\varphi)$ implies $\Occ(c,\varphi)$. (ii) $\Occ(c,\varphi)$ implies $\Occ^{+}(c,\varphi)$ or $\Occ^{-}(c,\varphi)$. (iii) If $\varphi$ is positive, no name occurs negatively in $\varphi$.
\end{lemma}

\subsection{Semantics}

\begin{definition}[Evaluation]
Given a \emph{base valuation} $v : A \to \{\text{true},\text{false}\}$ and a \emph{name assignment} $w : I \to \{\text{true},\text{false}\}$, put $\evalb{a}_{v,w} = v(a)$, $\evalb{\bot} = \text{false}$, $\evalb{\varphi \to \psi} = (\evalb{\varphi} \Rightarrow \evalb{\psi})$, $\evalb{Tc} = w(c)$.
\end{definition}

For a set $S$ of formulas, $(v,w) \models S$ means all members are true at $(v,w)$; and $S \models \psi$ means every $(v,w)$ satisfying $S$ satisfies $\psi$.

\begin{lemma}[Truth-free invariance]\label{lem:trfree}
If $\varphi$ is truth-free then $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w} = \evalb{\varphi}_{v,w'}$ for all $w,w'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Occurrence locality]\label{lem:local}
If $w(c) = w'(c)$ for every $c$ occurring in $\varphi$, then $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w} = \evalb{\varphi}_{v,w'}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polarity monotonicity]\label{lem:mono}
Suppose $w \le w'$ pointwise. If $\varphi$ is positive then $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w}$ implies $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w'}$; if $\varphi$ is negative then $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w'}$ implies $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Simultaneous induction on $\varphi$, the two statements swapping roles at the antecedent of an implication. The case $Tc$ is the hypothesis $w \le w'$ in one direction and vacuous in the other, since $Tc$ is never negative.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Polarized shift]\label{lem:shift}
Let $w,w'$ satisfy: for every $c$ occurring positively in $\varphi$, $w(c)$ implies $w'(c)$; and for every $c$ occurring negatively in $\varphi$, $w'(c)$ implies $w(c)$. Then $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w}$ implies $\evalb{\varphi}_{v,w'}$.
\end{lemma}

\section{Tangled hierarchies}

\begin{definition}[Tangled hierarchy]
A \emph{tangled hierarchy} on $(A,I)$ is a function $\den : I \to \Frm(A,I)$; $\den(c)$ is the \emph{sentence named by} $c$. No constraint is imposed: $\den(c)$ may contain $Tc$, and the \emph{dependency relation}
\[
  c' \prec c \quad :\Longleftrightarrow \quad \Occ(c', \den(c))
\]
may contain cycles of any length, including self-loops.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tarski theory]
$\Tar(\den) = \{\, Tc \leftrightarrow \den(c) : c \in I \,\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Model]
Given $v$, an assignment $w$ is a \emph{model} of $\den$ over $v$ if $w(c) \Leftrightarrow \evalb{\den(c)}_{v,w}$ for every $c$. Write $\Mod_v(\den)$ for the set of such $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:sat}
$(v,w) \models \Tar(\den)$ if and only if $w \in \Mod_v(\den)$.
\end{lemma}

So $\Mod_v(\den)$ is the solution set of a system of simultaneous fixed-point equations in the unknowns $w(c)$, with $v$ as parameter.

\begin{definition}[Conservativity]
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a set of truth-free formulas. The tangle $\den$ is \emph{conservative over} $\mathcal{T}$ if for every truth-free $\psi$,
\[
  \mathcal{T} \cup \Tar(\den) \models \psi \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \mathcal{T} \models \psi.
\]
It is \emph{conservative} if it is conservative over every truth-free $\mathcal{T}$.
\end{definition}

Taking $\psi = \bot$ shows that conservativity implies relative consistency.

\section{The exact criterion}

\begin{theorem}[Conservativity from expandability]\label{thm:expand}
If every base valuation $v$ admits some $w \in \Mod_v(\den)$, then $\den$ is conservative over every truth-free base theory.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $\mathcal{T},\psi$ be truth-free and suppose $\mathcal{T} \cup \Tar(\den) \models \psi$. Take $(v,w) \models \mathcal{T}$ and choose $w' \in \Mod_v(\den)$. Then $(v,w') \models \mathcal{T}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:trfree} and $(v,w') \models \Tar(\den)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:sat}, so $\evalb{\psi}_{v,w'}$ holds; by Lemma~\ref{lem:trfree} again $\evalb{\psi}_{v,w}$ holds. Hence $\mathcal{T} \models \psi$. The converse implication is monotonicity of entailment.
\end{proof}

The \emph{diagram} of $v$ is $\Diag(v) = \{\varphi : \varphi \text{ truth-free and true at } v\}$; it is a truth-free theory satisfied by $(v,w)$ for every $w$, and any model of it has $v$'s atomic values.

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of conservativity]\label{thm:char}
For any tangled hierarchy $\den$ the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item every base valuation $v$ admits a model $w \in \Mod_v(\den)$;
\item $\den$ is conservative over every truth-free base theory.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$(1)\Rightarrow(2)$ is Theorem~\ref{thm:expand}. For $(2)\Rightarrow(1)$, suppose $\Mod_v(\den) = \varnothing$ for some $v$. Any $(v',w')$ satisfying $\Diag(v) \cup \Tar(\den)$ has $v'$ agreeing with $v$ atomwise, so $w'$ would be a model of $\den$ over $v$ --- impossible. Hence $\Diag(v) \cup \Tar(\den)$ has no model and entails $\bot$, whereas $\Diag(v) \not\models \bot$ since $(v, \lambda c.\,\text{false})$ satisfies it. Conservativity fails for $\mathcal{T} = \Diag(v)$, $\psi = \bot$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Conservativity of a tangled hierarchy is not a subtle proof-theoretic property; it \emph{is} the solvability of the loop equations, uniformly in the state of the base. Every subsequent theorem is a structural sufficient condition for solvability.
\end{remark}

\section{Positive tangles: Knaster--Tarski}

Order assignments pointwise; the assignments form a complete lattice.

\begin{definition}[Revision operator]
For a positive tangle and a base valuation $v$, set $R_v(w)(c) = \evalb{\den(c)}_{v,w}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
If every $\den(c)$ is positive then $R_v$ is monotone.
\end{lemma}

By Knaster--Tarski, $R_v$ has a least fixed point $\lfp(R_v)$ and a greatest fixed point $\gfp(R_v)$, and $w \in \Mod_v(\den)$ iff $R_v(w) = w$.

\begin{theorem}[Conservativity of positive tangles]\label{thm:pos}
If every sentence of a tangled hierarchy is positive, the hierarchy has a model over every base valuation, hence is conservative over every truth-free base theory; in particular a consistent truth-free theory remains consistent after tangling.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
Nothing is assumed about the reference graph: a name may denote a sentence about itself, and the graph may be a single enormous strongly connected component.
\end{remark}

\section{Grounded tangles: existence and uniqueness}

\begin{definition}[Grounded]
$\den$ is \emph{grounded} with rank $\rk : I \to \mathbb{N}$ if $\Occ(c', \den(c))$ implies $\rk(c') < \rk(c)$.
\end{definition}

Define the revision sequence $R^0 = \lambda c.\,\text{false}$, $R^{n+1}(c) = \evalb{\den(c)}_{v,R^n}$.

\begin{lemma}[Stabilization]\label{lem:stab}
If $\den$ is grounded with rank $\rk$, then $R^n(c) = R^m(c)$ for all $n,m > \rk(c)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Strong induction on $n$: by Lemma~\ref{lem:local}, $R^{n+1}(c)$ depends only on $R^n(c')$ for names $c'$ of strictly smaller rank.
\end{proof}

Put $w^{\mathrm{st}}(c) = R^{\rk(c)+1}(c)$.

\begin{theorem}[Determinacy]\label{thm:groundeduniq}
If $\den$ is grounded then for every $v$ there is exactly one model, namely $w^{\mathrm{st}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Existence: unfold and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:stab} to the names occurring in $\den(c)$, each of smaller rank. Uniqueness: for any model $w$, prove $w(c) = w^{\mathrm{st}}(c)$ by strong induction on $\rk(c)$, using Lemma~\ref{lem:local}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conservativity]\label{thm:groundedcons}
A grounded tangled hierarchy, of arbitrary polarity, is conservative over every truth-free base theory.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Naming the old language]\label{cor:naming}
If every $\den(c)$ is truth-free, the biconditionals $Tc \leftrightarrow \den(c)$ --- stating that the internal truth predicate is sound and complete for the named old sentences --- are conservative over every truth-free base theory, and the truth predicate is uniquely determined by the base valuation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
A truth-free formula contains no name, so $\rk \equiv 0$ grounds the tangle vacuously.
\end{proof}

This is the exact sense in which internal soundness for the old theory costs nothing: no new theorem, and not even a new degree of freedom.

\section{Local stratification: loops inside a level}

\begin{definition}[Locally stratified]
$\den$ is \emph{locally stratified} by $\rk : I \to \mathbb{N}$ if
\begin{align*}
 \text{(neg)}\quad & \Occ^{-}(c', \den(c)) \implies \rk(c') < \rk(c),\\
 \text{(pos)}\quad & \Occ^{+}(c', \den(c)) \implies \rk(c') \le \rk(c).
\end{align*}
\end{definition}

Loops are permitted within a level; only negative dependencies must strictly descend. By Lemma~\ref{lem:polocc}(ii), every occurrence satisfies $\rk(c') \le \rk(c)$.

\begin{definition}[Level operator]
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and an assignment $A$ (the levels already built), set
\[
  L_{n,A}(w)(c) =
  \begin{cases}
    \evalb{\den(c)}_{v,\, \lambda c'.\,(\text{if } \rk(c') < n \text{ then } A(c') \text{ else } w(c'))} & \text{if } \rk(c) \le n,\\
    \text{false} & \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
If $\den$ is locally stratified by $\rk$, then $L_{n,A}$ is monotone.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:shift} to $\den(c)$ for $\rk(c) \le n$. A positively occurring $c'$ is either frozen at $A(c')$ or contributes $w(c')$, which increases with $w$. A negatively occurring $c'$ has $\rk(c') < \rk(c) \le n$ by (neg), hence is frozen and does not move.
\end{proof}

Let $F_0 = \lambda c.\,\text{false}$, $F_{n+1} = \lfp(L_{n,F_n})$, and $w^{\mathrm{loc}}(c) = F_{\rk(c)+1}(c)$. A stability lemma (induction on levels) gives $F_m(c) = F_{\rk(c)+1}(c)$ for all $m > \rk(c)$, so the levels glue and $w^{\mathrm{loc}}$ solves every loop equation.

\begin{theorem}[Local stratification implies conservativity]\label{thm:locstrat}
Every locally stratified tangled hierarchy has a model over every base valuation, and is therefore conservative over every truth-free base theory: an arbitrarily tangled level may be bolted onto a theory without changing a single old consequence.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Both earlier theorems are special cases]
A positive tangle is locally stratified by the constant rank $0$ (no negative occurrences, by Lemma~\ref{lem:polocc}(iii)); a grounded tangle is locally stratified by its own rank.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Strictness]\label{prop:strict}
Let $I = \{p,q\}$ with $\den(q) = \bot$ and $\den(p) = Tq \to Tp$. Then $\den$ is locally stratified by $\rk(q)=0$, $\rk(p)=1$; it is not positive ($q$ occurs negatively in $\den(p)$); and it is not grounded ($p$ occurs in $\den(p)$). Hence it is conservative by Theorem~\ref{thm:locstrat}, while neither Theorem~\ref{thm:pos} nor Theorem~\ref{thm:groundedcons} applies.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Non-necessity]\label{prop:nonnec}
Let $I = \{c\}$ with $\den(c) = Tc \to Tc$. Then $c$ occurs both positively and negatively in its own sentence, so no rank locally stratifies it; nevertheless every assignment is a model, so the tangle is conservative.
\end{proposition}

\section{Well-founded tangles and the collapse of height}

\begin{theorem}[Determinacy of well-founded tangles]\label{thm:wf}
If $\prec$ is well-founded then for every base valuation there is exactly one model, whatever the polarities.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Define the truth value at $c$ by recursion along $\prec$, evaluating $\den(c)$ against the values already defined at the names it mentions (all $\prec$-below $c$); this partial-assignment evaluation agrees with ordinary evaluation once the assignment is total. Uniqueness is $\prec$-induction with Lemma~\ref{lem:local}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
A well-founded tangled hierarchy of arbitrary height and polarity is conservative over every truth-free base theory.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Height collapse]\label{thm:collapse}
For any tangled hierarchy, $\prec$ is well-founded if and only if there is $\rk : I \to \mathbb{N}$ with $\Occ(c',\den(c)) \Rightarrow \rk(c') < \rk(c)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Leftarrow$) A relation embedding into $<$ on $\mathbb{N}$ is well-founded. ($\Rightarrow$) Each formula mentions finitely many names, so
$\rk(c) = 1 + \max\{\rk(c') : c' \text{ occurs in } \den(c)\}$
is a legitimate definition by $\prec$-recursion (empty maximum $=0$) and strictly descends.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
A finitary tangled hierarchy may be infinitely tall --- ranks unbounded --- but never transfinitely tall: no name sits at level $\omega$ or beyond.
\end{remark}

\begin{example}[Infinitely tall, nowhere positive, fully determined]
Let $I = \mathbb{N} \sqcup \{\star\}$ with $\den(0) = \bot$, $\den(n+1) = \neg Tn$, $\den(\star) = T0$. Every link is a negation and the ranks are unbounded; the tangle is well-founded, hence conservative, and determined: $T0$ false, $T1$ true, $T2$ false, \dots, with $T\star$ false. Infinite regress is not vicious circularity.
\end{example}

\section{The price of a strange loop: indeterminacy, measured}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-point description]
For a positive tangle, $\Mod_v(\den)$ is exactly the fixed-point set of $R_v$; hence $\lfp(R_v)$ and $\gfp(R_v)$ are models and every model $w$ satisfies $\lfp(R_v) \le w \le \gfp(R_v)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Determinacy criterion]\label{thm:determinacy}
A positive tangle has a unique model over $v$ if and only if $\lfp(R_v) = \gfp(R_v)$.
\end{theorem}

The minimal extension is the \emph{sceptical} truth predicate (assert only what is forced), the maximal one the \emph{credulous} predicate (assert everything not forbidden).

\begin{theorem}[Exponential semantics, zero syntax]\label{thm:loops}
Let $\den(c_i) = Tc_i$ for $i = 1,\dots,k$ (independent truth-tellers). Then: (1) every assignment is a model, so $|\Mod_v| = 2^k$; (2) the tangled theory decides neither $Tc_i$ nor $\neg Tc_i$; (3) for every truth-free $\mathcal{T}$ and truth-free $\psi$, $\mathcal{T} \cup \Tar(\den) \models \psi$ iff $\mathcal{T} \models \psi$; (4) for $k \ge 1$, $\lfp(R_v) \ne \gfp(R_v)$, the former declaring every loop false and the latter declaring them all true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The cost of one loop]\label{thm:trich}
For a tangle on a single name $c$ and any base valuation,
\[
  |\Mod(\den(c) = \bot)| = 1, \qquad |\Mod(\den(c) = Tc)| = 2, \qquad |\Mod(\den(c) = \neg Tc)| = 0 .
\]
A grounded denotation pins the truth predicate down; a positive self-loop leaves exactly one bit free; a negative self-loop is unsatisfiable.
\end{theorem}

\section{Sharpness: the liar}

\begin{theorem}[The liar is not conservative]\label{thm:liar}
Let $I = \{c\}$ and $\den(c) = \neg Tc$. Then $\Tar(\den) \models \bot$ while the empty theory is consistent; hence the liar tangle is conservative over no truth-free base theory.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A model would satisfy $w(c) \Leftrightarrow \neg w(c)$, impossible; a theory without models entails everything. The empty theory is satisfied by any valuation.
\end{proof}

Combined with Theorem~\ref{thm:char}, this shows each positive theorem is sharp in its own direction: the liar violates exactly the clause discarded in each case.

\section{Algorithms}

Let the tangle be finite with $n = |I|$ names and total sentence size $s$.

\paragraph{Model enumeration.} For arbitrary polarity, enumerate all $2^n$ assignments and test the $n$ loop equations: $O(2^n s)$. This is the reference implementation.

\paragraph{Kleene iteration.} For positive tangles, $R_v$ is monotone on a lattice of height $n$, so iterating upward from the all-false assignment reaches $\lfp(R_v)$ in at most $n$ steps, and downward from all-true reaches $\gfp(R_v)$; cost $O(ns)$ each. By Theorem~\ref{thm:determinacy} this gives a linear-time determinacy test without enumerating models.

\paragraph{Local stratification check.} Polarized occurrence data is computed in $O(s)$. A valid rank exists iff no strongly connected component of the dependency graph contains a negative edge; contract components and take the position in a topological order. Equivalently, solve the difference-constraint system (strict on negative edges, non-strict on positive ones) by a shortest-path computation in $O(n|E|)$.

\paragraph{Level construction.} Given a valid rank, process levels in increasing order, freezing all lower levels and running Kleene iteration within the level; total $O(ns)$. The resulting model is a \emph{certificate of conservativity} by Theorems~\ref{thm:locstrat} and~\ref{thm:expand}.

\section{Applications and interpretation}

\paragraph{Recursive and inductive definitions.} The revision operator is the one-step operator of a system of mutually recursive definitions, and positivity is exactly the condition making it monotone. Theorem~\ref{thm:pos} says such a system is a definitional extension in the strongest sense: it decides nothing new about the old vocabulary.

\paragraph{Stratified negation.} The database and logic-programming discipline ``no recursion through negation'' is the practitioner's version of local stratification. Theorem~\ref{thm:locstrat} identifies what it buys (solvability, hence conservativity) and Proposition~\ref{prop:nonnec} shows it is sufficient, not necessary.

\paragraph{Reflection principles.} Corollary~\ref{cor:naming} is the propositional shadow of a reflection principle for the old language: internal soundness and completeness for named old sentences is free. In the arithmetized setting reflection is famously non-conservative --- there the named sentences can express the naming apparatus itself, so the tangle is no longer grounded.

\paragraph{Self-describing data.} A knowledge base whose records assert the truth of other records is a tangled hierarchy. The design question is not ``are there cycles?'' but ``do the loop equations have a solution in every state of the base data?''.

\paragraph{The strange-loop thesis.} Strange loops do leave the levels above intact --- provided their negations are grounded. What a loop costs is not soundness but definiteness: a system with $k$ independent strange loops has $2^k$ equally admissible self-descriptions and no way to choose among them, while agreeing with the loop-free system on every statement about the world.

\section{Discussion and limitations}

The setting is propositional and self-reference is stipulated rather than constructed by a diagonal lemma; in an arithmetized setting the denotation function is itself definable, which introduces interactions invisible here. All results are semantic: a genuinely proof-theoretic version with derivation-size bounds is a separate question. Finally, the model-counting results concern very simple tangles; a general count for arbitrary finite positive tangles is open.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Syntactic conservativity via cut elimination]
For a locally stratified tangle there is a sequent calculus for the tangled language in which every derivation of a truth-free sequent from the Tarski biconditionals can be transformed, by a terminating rewriting on derivations, into a derivation using no biconditional --- with at most an exponential blow-up in size, and only a polynomial blow-up when the tangle is grounded.
\end{conjecture}

The level-by-level model construction should be the semantic shadow of a cut-elimination strategy eliminating truth atoms in order of decreasing rank: each least-fixed-point stage corresponds to saturating the positive loops of one level, which is where the exponential factor should appear.

\begin{conjecture}[Loop count = degrees of freedom]
For a finite positive tangle whose dependency digraph has $k$ strongly connected components containing a cycle, the model set is a complete lattice whose height is bounded by a function of $k$ alone, and the number of models is at most $2^{(\text{total size of the loops})}$, with equality iff every loop is a disjoint truth-teller. Conservativity is uniform in $k$: the syntactic cost stays $0$.
\end{conjecture}

Since the least and greatest fixed points bracket every model, all indeterminacy is concentrated in the interval between them, and that interval should factor as a product over the cyclic strongly connected components.

Further questions: quantified and first-order tangles; partial (three-valued) valuations, where the liar becomes a gap rather than an inconsistency; the complexity landscape (deciding solvability for arbitrary polarity encodes propositional satisfiability, and the structural conditions above are the polynomial-time islands); and a quantitative theory of tangle \emph{entropy} $\log_2 |\Mod_v|$, equal to $k$ bits for $k$ independent loops and $0$ for grounded tangles.

\section{Summary}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
Condition on the tangle & Models per valuation & Conservative? \\
\midrule
Arbitrary & --- & iff every valuation expands \\
Positive & $\ge 1$ & yes \\
Grounded ($\mathbb{N}$-rank, all edges descend) & exactly $1$ & yes \\
Locally stratified & $\ge 1$ & yes \\
Well-founded dependency & exactly $1$ & yes \\
$k$ independent truth-tellers & exactly $2^k$ & yes \\
Single name $\bot$ / $Tc$ / $\neg Tc$ & $1$ / $2$ / $0$ & yes / yes / \textbf{no} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Conservativity is solvability; solvability is guaranteed by monotonicity, by grounding, or by the hybrid of the two; and the entire cost of a strange loop is paid in indeterminacy, never in new theorems --- until the loop turns negative on itself, at which point nothing can be paid at all.

Conservativity for Tangled Hierarchies -- numerical demonstrations.

A *tangled hierarchy* is a propositional language with atoms a in A, falsum, and
implication, extended by an internal truth atom T c for every *name* c, together
with a denotation function den mapping each name c to a formula den(c) that may
mention T c itself.  Its theory is the family of Tarski biconditionals

        T c  <->  den(c)          (one for each name c).

A *model over a base valuation v* is an assignment w of truth values to names
solving all of these equations simultaneously.  The central theorem is:

        the tangle adds no new truth-free consequence to any truth-free base
        theory  <==>  every base valuation expands to a model.

This script implements the syntax, semantics, and every algorithm from the
development, and then verifies the quantitative results numerically:

  1. the single-name trichotomy  1 / 2 / 0  (grounded / truth-teller / liar);
  2. k independent strange loops have exactly 2^k models and add no theorem;
  3. positive tangles always have a model (Knaster-Tarski), checked by
     exhaustive enumeration over a large random sample;
  4. grounded and well-founded tangles have exactly one model;
  5. the mixed tangle:  locally stratified, but neither positive nor grounded;
  6. the tautological loop  T c -> T c:  conservative although not locally
     stratified -- local stratification is sufficient, not necessary;
  7. an exhaustive census of all small single-name denotations, exhibiting the
     exact correlation between negative self-reference and loss of models;
  8. a direct, brute-force conservativity audit over a finite base language.

Run with:  python3 demo.py

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Syntax
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Atom:
    """An atom of the old (truth-free) vocabulary."""

    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Fls:
    """Falsum."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Imp:
    """Implication."""

    left: "Frm"
    right: "Frm"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tr:
    """The internal truth atom of a name."""

    name: str


Frm = object  # union of Atom | Fls | Imp | Tr


def neg(phi: Frm) -> Frm:
    """Negation, encoded as `phi -> falsum`."""
    return Imp(phi, Fls())


def show(phi: Frm) -> str:
    """Readable rendering of a formula."""
    if isinstance(phi, Atom):
        return phi.name
    if isinstance(phi, Fls):
        return "⊥"
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return f"T{phi.name}"
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    if isinstance(phi.right, Fls):
        return f"¬{show(phi.left)}"
    return f"({show(phi.left)} → {show(phi.right)})"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.  Semantics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Valuation = Dict[str, bool]  # base atoms  -> truth values
Assignment = Dict[str, bool]  # names       -> truth values


def evaluate(phi: Frm, v: Valuation, w: Assignment) -> bool:
    """Truth value of `phi` under base valuation `v` and name assignment `w`."""
    if isinstance(phi, Atom):
        return v[phi.name]
    if isinstance(phi, Fls):
        return False
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return w[phi.name]
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return (not evaluate(phi.left, v, w)) or evaluate(phi.right, v, w)


def truth_free(phi: Frm) -> bool:
    """Does `phi` avoid the internal truth predicate entirely?"""
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return True
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return False
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return truth_free(phi.left) and truth_free(phi.right)


def occurs(c: str, phi: Frm) -> bool:
    """Does the name `c` occur in `phi`?"""
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return False
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return phi.name == c
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return occurs(c, phi.left) or occurs(c, phi.right)


def occurrences(phi: Frm) -> Set[str]:
    """All names occurring in `phi`."""
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return set()
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return {phi.name}
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return occurrences(phi.left) | occurrences(phi.right)


def occurs_pol(c: str, phi: Frm, positive: bool) -> bool:
    """Does `c` occur with the given polarity in `phi`?

    Positive = under an even number of antecedent positions.
    """
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return False
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return positive and phi.name == c
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return occurs_pol(c, phi.left, not positive) or occurs_pol(c, phi.right, positive)


def is_positive(phi: Frm) -> bool:
    """Is every truth atom of `phi` in positive position (no truth atom negated)?"""
    return all(not occurs_pol(c, phi, False) for c in occurrences(phi))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.  Tangled hierarchies
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Tangle = Dict[str, Frm]  # name -> the sentence it denotes


def is_model(den: Tangle, v: Valuation, w: Assignment) -> bool:
    """Does `w` solve every loop equation  w(c) <-> den(c)  over `v`?"""
    return all(w[c] == evaluate(den[c], v, w) for c in den)


def all_assignments(names: Sequence[str]) -> Iterable[Assignment]:
    """Every truth assignment to the given names."""
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(names)):
        yield dict(zip(names, bits))


def models(den: Tangle, v: Valuation) -> List[Assignment]:
    """ALGORITHM (brute force): all models of the tangle over `v`.  O(2^n * s)."""
    names = sorted(den)
    return [w for w in all_assignments(names) if is_model(den, v, w)]


def revise(den: Tangle, v: Valuation, w: Assignment) -> Assignment:
    """One application of the revision operator  R(w)(c) = [[den(c)]]_{v,w}."""
    return {c: evaluate(den[c], v, w) for c in den}


def kleene_lfp(den: Tangle, v: Valuation) -> Assignment:
    """ALGORITHM: least fixed point of a *positive* tangle, by Kleene iteration.

    Starts at the everywhere-false assignment and iterates the monotone revision
    operator; converges in at most |names| steps.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    w: Assignment = {c: False for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        w2 = revise(den, v, w)
        if w2 == w:
            return w
        w = w2
    return w


def kleene_gfp(den: Tangle, v: Valuation) -> Assignment:
    """ALGORITHM: greatest fixed point of a positive tangle, dually.  O(n * s)."""
    w: Assignment = {c: True for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        w2 = revise(den, v, w)
        if w2 == w:
            return w
        w = w2
    return w


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.  Structural conditions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def grounded_rank(den: Tangle) -> Optional[Dict[str, int]]:
    """ALGORITHM: a rank with strictly descending dependencies, if one exists.

    Equivalently (height collapse theorem) a witness that the dependency
    relation is well founded.  Computed by iterated relaxation; returns None if
    the dependency graph has a cycle.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    rank: Dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        changed = False
        for c in den:
            need = max((rank[d] + 1 for d in occurrences(den[c]) if d in den), default=0)
            if need > rank[c]:
                rank[c], changed = need, True
        if not changed:
            return rank
    return None


def local_stratification(den: Tangle) -> Optional[Dict[str, int]]:
    """ALGORITHM: a local stratification rank, if one exists.

    Requires  rk(c') <  rk(c)  for every NEGATIVE occurrence of c' in den(c),
    and       rk(c') <= rk(c)  for every POSITIVE occurrence.
    Solved as a difference-constraint system by Bellman-Ford style relaxation;
    returns None when a positive-weight cycle (a negative edge inside a strongly
    connected component) blocks all solutions.  Complexity O(n * |E|).
    """
    edges: List[Tuple[str, str, int]] = []  # (source name c', target name c, slack)
    for c, phi in den.items():
        for d in occurrences(phi):
            if d not in den:
                continue
            if occurs_pol(d, phi, False):
                edges.append((d, c, 1))
            if occurs_pol(d, phi, True):
                edges.append((d, c, 0))
    rank: Dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        changed = False
        for (src, tgt, slack) in edges:
            if rank[src] + slack > rank[tgt]:
                rank[tgt] = rank[src] + slack
                changed = True
        if not changed:
            return rank
    return None


def level_model(den: Tangle, rank: Dict[str, int], v: Valuation) -> Assignment:
    """ALGORITHM: the level-by-level model of a locally stratified tangle.

    Levels are processed in increasing rank; everything strictly below the
    current level is frozen at its computed value, and within the level the
    least fixed point of the (monotone) level operator is reached by Kleene
    iteration.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    built: Assignment = {c: False for c in den}
    for n in range(max(rank.values(), default=0) + 1):
        w: Assignment = {c: False for c in den}
        for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
            merged = {c: (built[c] if rank[c] < n else w[c]) for c in den}
            w2 = {c: (evaluate(den[c], v, merged) if rank[c] <= n else False) for c in den}
            if w2 == w:
                break
            w = w2
        built = w
    return built


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.  Conservativity auditing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def expandable_everywhere(den: Tangle, atoms: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
    """Does every base valuation over `atoms` expand to a model of the tangle?

    By the characterization theorem, this is *exactly* conservativity over every
    truth-free base theory.
    """
    return all(len(models(den, dict(zip(atoms, bits)))) > 0
               for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(atoms)))


def truth_free_formulas(atoms: Sequence[str], depth: int) -> List[Frm]:
    """All truth-free formulas of implication depth <= `depth` over `atoms`."""
    level: List[Frm] = [Fls()] + [Atom(a) for a in atoms]
    out: List[Frm] = list(level)
    for _ in range(depth):
        new = [Imp(p, q) for p in out for q in out]
        out = list({show(f): f for f in out + new}.values())
    return out


def entails_truthfree(theory: Sequence[Frm], psi: Frm, atoms: Sequence[str],
                      den: Optional[Tangle]) -> bool:
    """Semantic entailment, over the tangled theory when `den` is supplied.

    Quantifies over all base valuations and (if `den` is given) all name
    assignments satisfying the Tarski biconditionals.
    """
    names = sorted(den) if den else []
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(atoms)):
        v = dict(zip(atoms, bits))
        candidates = ([w for w in all_assignments(names) if is_model(den, v, w)]
                      if den else [{}])
        for w in candidates:
            if all(evaluate(phi, v, w) for phi in theory):
                if not evaluate(psi, v, w):
                    return False
    return True


def conservativity_audit(den: Tangle, atoms: Sequence[str], depth: int = 1) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Brute-force audit: compare old and tangled consequence for every pair
    (base theory drawn from the small truth-free formulas, truth-free target).

    Returns (number of pairs checked, number of discrepancies found).
    """
    pool = truth_free_formulas(atoms, depth)
    checked = 0
    bad = 0
    for theory_phi in pool:
        for psi in pool:
            old = entails_truthfree([theory_phi], psi, atoms, None)
            new = entails_truthfree([theory_phi], psi, atoms, den)
            checked += 1
            if old != new:
                bad += 1
    return checked, bad


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.  The demonstrations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print("\n" + "=" * 74)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 74)


def demo_trichotomy() -> None:
    """The cost of one loop:  grounded 1, truth-teller 2, liar 0 models."""
    banner("1.  THE COST OF ONE LOOP  (single-name trichotomy)")
    v: Valuation = {"a": True}
    cases = [("grounded   den(c) = ⊥", {"c": Fls()}, 1),
             ("truth-teller den(c) = Tc", {"c": Tr("c")}, 2),
             ("liar        den(c) = ¬Tc", {"c": neg(Tr("c"))}, 0)]
    for label, den, expected in cases:
        ms = models(den, v)
        print(f"  {label:28s}  models = {len(ms)}   (predicted {expected})")
        assert len(ms) == expected
    print("  ⇒ 1 / 2 / 0 confirmed: grounding buys determinacy, a positive loop")
    print("    costs one bit, a negative loop costs everything (no model at all).")


def demo_k_loops(kmax: int = 8) -> None:
    """k independent strange loops: 2^k models, and no new theorem."""
    banner("2.  k INDEPENDENT STRANGE LOOPS:  2^k MODELS, 0 NEW THEOREMS")
    v: Valuation = {"a": False}
    for k in range(kmax + 1):
        den: Tangle = {f"c{i}": Tr(f"c{i}") for i in range(k)}
        count = len(models(den, v))
        print(f"  k = {k:2d}   models = {count:4d}   2^k = {2 ** k:4d}   "
              f"conservative = {expandable_everywhere(den, ['a'])}")
        assert count == 2 ** k
    print("  ⇒ exponential in semantics, zero in syntax.")


def demo_extremal_extensions() -> None:
    """Sceptical vs credulous truth predicates, and the determinacy criterion."""
    banner("3.  EXTREMAL EXTENSIONS AND THE DETERMINACY CRITERION")
    v: Valuation = {"a": True}
    examples: List[Tuple[str, Tangle]] = [
        ("two independent loops", {"p": Tr("p"), "q": Tr("q")}),
        ("chained loop  p ↦ Tq,  q ↦ Tp", {"p": Tr("q"), "q": Tr("p")}),
        ("forced        p ↦ a,   q ↦ Tp", {"p": Atom("a"), "q": Tr("p")}),
        ("tautology     c ↦ Tc → Tc", {"c": Imp(Tr("c"), Tr("c"))}),
    ]
    for label, den in examples:
        lfp, gfp = kleene_lfp(den, v), kleene_gfp(den, v)
        unique = lfp == gfp
        print(f"  {label:32s} lfp={fmt(lfp)}  gfp={fmt(gfp)}  "
              f"models={len(models(den, v))}  determinate={unique}")
        assert unique == (len(models(den, v)) == 1)
    print("  ⇒ a positive tangle is determinate exactly when its minimal and")
    print("    maximal extensions of the truth predicate coincide.")


def fmt(w: Assignment) -> str:
    return "{" + ",".join(f"{c}:{'T' if w[c] else 'F'}" for c in sorted(w)) + "}"


def demo_structural_conditions() -> None:
    """Positive, grounded, locally stratified: which condition applies where."""
    banner("4.  POSITIVE / GROUNDED / LOCALLY STRATIFIED")
    atoms = ["a"]
    examples: List[Tuple[str, Tangle]] = [
        ("liar            c ↦ ¬Tc", {"c": neg(Tr("c"))}),
        ("truth-teller    c ↦ Tc", {"c": Tr("c")}),
        ("grounded        c ↦ a", {"c": Atom("a")}),
        ("mixed  q ↦ ⊥,  p ↦ Tq → Tp", {"q": Fls(), "p": Imp(Tr("q"), Tr("p"))}),
        ("tautology       c ↦ Tc → Tc", {"c": Imp(Tr("c"), Tr("c"))}),
        ("negated chain   p ↦ ¬Tq, q ↦ a", {"p": neg(Tr("q")), "q": Atom("a")}),
    ]
    header = f"  {'tangle':32s} {'pos':>5s} {'grnd':>5s} {'loc.str':>8s} {'models':>7s} {'consv':>6s}"
    print(header)
    print("  " + "-" * (len(header) - 2))
    for label, den in examples:
        pos = all(is_positive(phi) for phi in den.values())
        grd = grounded_rank(den) is not None
        loc = local_stratification(den) is not None
        counts = {len(models(den, dict(zip(atoms, bits))))
                  for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(atoms))}
        cons = expandable_everywhere(den, atoms)
        print(f"  {label:32s} {str(pos):>5s} {str(grd):>5s} {str(loc):>8s} "
              f"{str(sorted(counts)):>7s} {str(cons):>6s}")
        # Every sufficient condition really is sufficient:
        if pos or grd or loc:
            assert cons
    print("  ⇒ the mixed tangle is locally stratified but neither positive nor")
    print("    grounded; the tautology is conservative though nothing stratifies it;")
    print("    only the liar fails, and it fails by outright unsatisfiability.")


def demo_level_construction() -> None:
    """The level-by-level construction reproduces a genuine model."""
    banner("5.  LEVEL-BY-LEVEL CONSTRUCTION FOR A LOCALLY STRATIFIED TANGLE")
    den: Tangle = {
        "q": Fls(),                                  # level 0
        "r": Atom("a"),                              # level 0
        "p": Imp(Tr("q"), Tr("p")),                  # level 1: positive self-loop
        "s": Imp(neg(Tr("r")), Tr("s")),             # level 1: positive self-loop
    }
    rank = local_stratification(den)
    assert rank is not None
    print(f"  computed rank: {rank}")
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=1):
        v = {"a": bits[0]}
        w = level_model(den, rank, v)
        ok = is_model(den, v, w)
        print(f"  v(a) = {str(bits[0]):5s}  level model {fmt(w)}  solves every loop equation: {ok}"
              f"   (total models: {len(models(den, v))})")
        assert ok
    print("  ⇒ freeze the lower levels, take the least fixed point inside the level,")
    print("    glue: the construction is linear in the size of the tangle.")


def demo_omega_tangle(height: int = 12) -> None:
    """An infinitely tall, nowhere positive, completely determined tangle."""
    banner("6.  AN INFINITELY TALL TANGLE  (truncated at finite height)")
    den: Tangle = {"n0": Fls()}
    for n in range(1, height):
        den[f"n{n}"] = neg(Tr(f"n{n - 1}"))
    den["star"] = Tr("n0")
    v: Valuation = {"a": True}
    rank = grounded_rank(den)
    assert rank is not None
    ms = models(den, v)
    assert len(ms) == 1
    w = ms[0]
    pattern = "".join("T" if w[f"n{n}"] else "F" for n in range(height))
    print(f"  height {height}: unique model, T-values along the tower: {pattern}")
    print(f"  T(star) = {w['star']};  every link is a negation, so the tangle is nowhere positive:")
    print(f"  positive = {all(is_positive(p) for p in den.values())}, "
          f"well-founded rank exists = {rank is not None}")
    print("  ⇒ infinite regress is not vicious circularity: unbounded height,")
    print("    no positivity anywhere, and still exactly one truth predicate.")


def enumerate_small_denotations(depth: int) -> List[Frm]:
    """All formulas over {a, ⊥, Tc} of implication depth <= `depth`."""
    out: List[Frm] = [Fls(), Atom("a"), Tr("c")]
    for _ in range(depth):
        new = [Imp(p, q) for p in out for q in out]
        out = list({show(f): f for f in out + new}.values())
    return out


def demo_census(depth: int = 2) -> None:
    """Exhaustive census of small single-name tangles."""
    banner("7.  EXHAUSTIVE CENSUS OF SMALL SINGLE-NAME TANGLES")
    pool = enumerate_small_denotations(depth)
    census: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
    positive_without_model = 0
    lost_model_and_positive = 0
    lost_model_total = 0
    for phi in pool:
        counts = tuple(len(models({"c": phi}, {"a": b})) for b in (False, True))
        census[counts] = census.get(counts, 0) + 1
        if min(counts) == 0:
            lost_model_total += 1
            if is_positive(phi):
                positive_without_model += 1
                lost_model_and_positive += 1
    print(f"  denotations of depth ≤ {depth} over {{a, ⊥, Tc}}: {len(pool)}")
    print("  distribution of (#models at v(a)=F, #models at v(a)=T):")
    for key in sorted(census, key=lambda k: -census[k]):
        print(f"      {key} : {census[key]}")
    print(f"  denotations losing a model for some valuation: {lost_model_total}")
    print(f"  ... of which positive: {positive_without_model}  (theory predicts 0)")
    assert positive_without_model == 0
    mixed = sum(1 for phi in pool
                if len({len(models({'c': phi}, {'a': b})) for b in (False, True)}) > 1)
    print(f"  denotations whose model count DEPENDS on the base valuation: {mixed}")
    print("  ⇒ every positive denotation is solvable for every valuation, and")
    print("    conservativity genuinely has to be stated per valuation.")


def demo_conservativity_audit() -> None:
    """Brute-force check that conservative tangles prove nothing new."""
    banner("8.  BRUTE-FORCE CONSERVATIVITY AUDIT")
    atoms = ["a", "b"]
    cases: List[Tuple[str, Tangle]] = [
        ("truth-teller  c ↦ Tc", {"c": Tr("c")}),
        ("two loops     p ↦ Tp, q ↦ Tq", {"p": Tr("p"), "q": Tr("q")}),
        ("mixed  q ↦ ⊥, p ↦ Tq → Tp", {"q": Fls(), "p": Imp(Tr("q"), Tr("p"))}),
        ("naming  c ↦ (a → b)", {"c": Imp(Atom("a"), Atom("b"))}),
        ("LIAR          c ↦ ¬Tc", {"c": neg(Tr("c"))}),
    ]
    for label, den in cases:
        checked, bad = conservativity_audit(den, atoms, depth=1)
        verdict = "CONSERVATIVE" if bad == 0 else f"NOT conservative ({bad} discrepancies)"
        print(f"  {label:34s} pairs checked = {checked:5d}   {verdict}")
        assert (bad == 0) == expandable_everywhere(den, atoms)
    print("  ⇒ the audit agrees exactly with the criterion: a tangle proves")
    print("    something new precisely when some valuation admits no model.")


def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__.strip().splitlines()[0])
    demo_trichotomy()
    demo_k_loops()
    demo_extremal_extensions()
    demo_structural_conditions()
    demo_level_construction()
    demo_omega_tangle()
    demo_census()
    demo_conservativity_audit()
    banner("ALL DEMONSTRATIONS COMPLETED — every predicted count was confirmed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Syntax
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Atom:
    """An atom of the old (truth-free) vocabulary."""

    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Fls:
    """Falsum."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Imp:
    """Implication."""

    left: "Frm"
    right: "Frm"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tr:
    """The internal truth atom of a name."""

    name: str


Frm = object  # union of Atom | Fls | Imp | Tr


def neg(phi: Frm) -> Frm:
    """Negation, encoded as `phi -> falsum`."""
    return Imp(phi, Fls())


def show(phi: Frm) -> str:
    """Readable rendering of a formula."""
    if isinstance(phi, Atom):
        return phi.name
    if isinstance(phi, Fls):
        return "⊥"
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return f"T{phi.name}"
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    if isinstance(phi.right, Fls):
        return f"¬{show(phi.left)}"
    return f"({show(phi.left)} → {show(phi.right)})"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.  Semantics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Valuation = Dict[str, bool]  # base atoms  -> truth values
Assignment = Dict[str, bool]  # names       -> truth values


def evaluate(phi: Frm, v: Valuation, w: Assignment) -> bool:
    """Truth value of `phi` under base valuation `v` and name assignment `w`."""
    if isinstance(phi, Atom):
        return v[phi.name]
    if isinstance(phi, Fls):
        return False
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return w[phi.name]
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return (not evaluate(phi.left, v, w)) or evaluate(phi.right, v, w)


def truth_free(phi: Frm) -> bool:
    """Does `phi` avoid the internal truth predicate entirely?"""
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return True
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return False
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return truth_free(phi.left) and truth_free(phi.right)


def occurs(c: str, phi: Frm) -> bool:
    """Does the name `c` occur in `phi`?"""
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return False
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return phi.name == c
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return occurs(c, phi.left) or occurs(c, phi.right)


def occurrences(phi: Frm) -> Set[str]:
    """All names occurring in `phi`."""
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return set()
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return {phi.name}
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return occurrences(phi.left) | occurrences(phi.right)


def occurs_pol(c: str, phi: Frm, positive: bool) -> bool:
    """Does `c` occur with the given polarity in `phi`?

    Positive = under an even number of antecedent positions.
    """
    if isinstance(phi, (Atom, Fls)):
        return False
    if isinstance(phi, Tr):
        return positive and phi.name == c
    assert isinstance(phi, Imp)
    return occurs_pol(c, phi.left, not positive) or occurs_pol(c, phi.right, positive)


def is_positive(phi: Frm) -> bool:
    """Is every truth atom of `phi` in positive position (no truth atom negated)?"""
    return all(not occurs_pol(c, phi, False) for c in occurrences(phi))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.  Tangled hierarchies
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Tangle = Dict[str, Frm]  # name -> the sentence it denotes


def is_model(den: Tangle, v: Valuation, w: Assignment) -> bool:
    """Does `w` solve every loop equation  w(c) <-> den(c)  over `v`?"""
    return all(w[c] == evaluate(den[c], v, w) for c in den)


def all_assignments(names: Sequence[str]) -> Iterable[Assignment]:
    """Every truth assignment to the given names."""
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(names)):
        yield dict(zip(names, bits))


def models(den: Tangle, v: Valuation) -> List[Assignment]:
    """ALGORITHM (brute force): all models of the tangle over `v`.  O(2^n * s)."""
    names = sorted(den)
    return [w for w in all_assignments(names) if is_model(den, v, w)]


def revise(den: Tangle, v: Valuation, w: Assignment) -> Assignment:
    """One application of the revision operator  R(w)(c) = [[den(c)]]_{v,w}."""
    return {c: evaluate(den[c], v, w) for c in den}


def kleene_lfp(den: Tangle, v: Valuation) -> Assignment:
    """ALGORITHM: least fixed point of a *positive* tangle, by Kleene iteration.

    Starts at the everywhere-false assignment and iterates the monotone revision
    operator; converges in at most |names| steps.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    w: Assignment = {c: False for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        w2 = revise(den, v, w)
        if w2 == w:
            return w
        w = w2
    return w


def kleene_gfp(den: Tangle, v: Valuation) -> Assignment:
    """ALGORITHM: greatest fixed point of a positive tangle, dually.  O(n * s)."""
    w: Assignment = {c: True for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        w2 = revise(den, v, w)
        if w2 == w:
            return w
        w = w2
    return w


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.  Structural conditions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def grounded_rank(den: Tangle) -> Optional[Dict[str, int]]:
    """ALGORITHM: a rank with strictly descending dependencies, if one exists.

    Equivalently (height collapse theorem) a witness that the dependency
    relation is well founded.  Computed by iterated relaxation; returns None if
    the dependency graph has a cycle.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    rank: Dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        changed = False
        for c in den:
            need = max((rank[d] + 1 for d in occurrences(den[c]) if d in den), default=0)
            if need > rank[c]:
                rank[c], changed = need, True
        if not changed:
            return rank
    return None


def local_stratification(den: Tangle) -> Optional[Dict[str, int]]:
    """ALGORITHM: a local stratification rank, if one exists.

    Requires  rk(c') <  rk(c)  for every NEGATIVE occurrence of c' in den(c),
    and       rk(c') <= rk(c)  for every POSITIVE occurrence.
    Solved as a difference-constraint system by Bellman-Ford style relaxation;
    returns None when a positive-weight cycle (a negative edge inside a strongly
    connected component) blocks all solutions.  Complexity O(n * |E|).
    """
    edges: List[Tuple[str, str, int]] = []  # (source name c', target name c, slack)
    for c, phi in den.items():
        for d in occurrences(phi):
            if d not in den:
                continue
            if occurs_pol(d, phi, False):
                edges.append((d, c, 1))
            if occurs_pol(d, phi, True):
                edges.append((d, c, 0))
    rank: Dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in den}
    for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
        changed = False
        for (src, tgt, slack) in edges:
            if rank[src] + slack > rank[tgt]:
                rank[tgt] = rank[src] + slack
                changed = True
        if not changed:
            return rank
    return None


def level_model(den: Tangle, rank: Dict[str, int], v: Valuation) -> Assignment:
    """ALGORITHM: the level-by-level model of a locally stratified tangle.

    Levels are processed in increasing rank; everything strictly below the
    current level is frozen at its computed value, and within the level the
    least fixed point of the (monotone) level operator is reached by Kleene
    iteration.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    built: Assignment = {c: False for c in den}
    for n in range(max(rank.values(), default=0) + 1):
        w: Assignment = {c: False for c in den}
        for _ in range(len(den) + 1):
            merged = {c: (built[c] if rank[c] < n else w[c]) for c in den}
            w2 = {c: (evaluate(den[c], v, merged) if rank[c] <= n else False) for c in den}
            if w2 == w:
                break
            w = w2
        built = w
    return built


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.  Conservativity auditing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def expandable_everywhere(den: Tangle, atoms: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
    """Does every base valuation over `atoms` expand to a model of the tangle?

    By the characterization theorem, this is *exactly* conservativity over every
    truth-free base theory.
    """
    return all(len(models(den, dict(zip(atoms, bits)))) > 0
               for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(atoms)))


def truth_free_formulas(atoms: Sequence[str], depth: int) -> List[Frm]:
    """All truth-free formulas of implication depth <= `depth` over `atoms`."""
    level: List[Frm] = [Fls()] + [Atom(a) for a in atoms]
    out: List[Frm] = list(level)
    for _ in range(depth):
        new = [Imp(p, q) for p in out for q in out]
        out = list({show(f): f for f in out + new}.values())
    return out


def entails_truthfree(theory: Sequence[Frm], psi: Frm, atoms: Sequence[str],
                      den: Optional[Tangle]) -> bool:
    """Semantic entailment, over the tangled theory when `den` is supplied.

    Quantifies over all base valuations and (if `den` is given) all name
    assignments satisfying the Tarski biconditionals.
    """
    names = sorted(den) if den else []
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(atoms)):
        v = dict(zip(atoms, bits))
        candidates = ([w for w in all_assignments(names) if is_model(den, v, w)]
                      if den else [{}])
        for w in candidates:
            if all(evaluate(phi, v, w) for phi in theory):
                if not evaluate(psi, v, w):
                    return False
    return True


def conservativity_audit(den: Tangle, atoms: Sequence[str], depth: int = 1) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Brute-force audit: compare old and tangled consequence for every pair
    (base theory drawn from the small truth-free formulas, truth-free target).

    Returns (number of pairs checked, number of discrepancies found).
    """
    pool = truth_free_formulas(atoms, depth)
    checked = 0
    bad = 0
    for theory_phi in pool:
        for psi in pool:
            old = entails_truthfree([theory_phi], psi, atoms, None)
            new = entails_truthfree([theory_phi], psi, atoms, den)
            checked += 1
            if old != new:
                bad += 1
    return checked, bad

def demo_structural_conditions() -> None:
    """Positive, grounded, locally stratified: which condition applies where."""
    banner("4.  POSITIVE / GROUNDED / LOCALLY STRATIFIED")
    atoms = ["a"]
    examples: List[Tuple[str, Tangle]] = [
        ("liar            c ↦ ¬Tc", {"c": neg(Tr("c"))}),
        ("truth-teller    c ↦ Tc", {"c": Tr("c")}),
        ("grounded        c ↦ a", {"c": Atom("a")}),
        ("mixed  q ↦ ⊥,  p ↦ Tq → Tp", {"q": Fls(), "p": Imp(Tr("q"), Tr("p"))}),
        ("tautology       c ↦ Tc → Tc", {"c": Imp(Tr("c"), Tr("c"))}),
        ("negated chain   p ↦ ¬Tq, q ↦ a", {"p": neg(Tr("q")), "q": Atom("a")}),
    ]
    header = f"  {'tangle':32s} {'pos':>5s} {'grnd':>5s} {'loc.str':>8s} {'models':>7s} {'consv':>6s}"
    print(header)
    print("  " + "-" * (len(header) - 2))
    for label, den in examples:
        pos = all(is_positive(phi) for phi in den.values())
        grd = grounded_rank(den) is not None

        counts = {len(models(den, dict(zip(atoms, bits))))

        print(f"  {label:32s} {str(pos):>5s} {str(grd):>5s} {str(loc):>8s} "

    print("  ⇒ the mixed tangle is locally stratified but neither positive nor")
    print("    grounded; the tautology is conservative though nothing stratifies it;")
    print("    only the liar fails, and it fails by outright unsatisfiability.")


def demo_level_construction() -> None:
    """The level-by-level construction reproduces a genuine model."""
    banner("5.  LEVEL-BY-LEVEL CONSTRUCTION FOR A LOCALLY STRATIFIED TANGLE")
    den: Tangle = {
        "q": Fls(),                                  # level 0
        "r": Atom("a"),                              # level 0

def demo_omega_tangle(height: int = 12) -> None:
    """An infinitely tall, nowhere positive, completely determined tangle."""
    banner("6.  AN INFINITELY TALL TANGLE  (truncated at finite height)")
    den: Tangle = {"n0": Fls()}
    for n in range(1, height):
        den[f"n{n}"] = neg(Tr(f"n{n - 1}"))
    den["star"] = Tr("n0")
    v: Valuation = {"a": True}
    rank = grounded_rank(den)
    assert rank is not None
    ms = models(den, v)
    assert len(ms) == 1
    w = ms[0]
    pattern = "".join("T" if w[f"n{n}"] else "F" for n in range(height))
    print(f"  height {height}: unique model, T-values along the tower: {pattern}")
    print(f"  T(star) = {w['star']};  every link is a negation, so the tangle is nowhere positive:")
    print(f"  positive = {all(is_positive(p) for p in den.values())}, "
          f"well-founded rank exists = {rank is not None}")
    print("  ⇒ infinite regress is not vicious circularity: unbounded height,")
    print("    no positivity anywhere, and still exactly one truth predicate.")


def enumerate_small_denotations(depth: int) -> List[Frm]:
    """All formulas over {a, ⊥, Tc} of implication depth <= `depth`."""
    out: List[Frm] = [Fls(), Atom("a"), Tr("c")]
    for _ in range(depth):
        new = [Imp(p, q) for p in out for q in out]
        out = list({show(f): f for f in out + new}.values())
    return out


def demo_census(depth: int = 2) -> None:
    """Exhaustive census of small single-name tangles."""
    banner("7.  EXHAUSTIVE CENSUS OF SMALL SINGLE-NAME TANGLES")
    pool = enumerate_small_denotations(depth)
    census: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
    positive_without_model = 0
    lost_model_and_positive = 0
    lost_model_total = 0
    for phi in pool:
        counts = tuple(len(models({"c": phi}, {"a": b})) for b in (False, True))
        census[counts] = census.get(counts, 0) + 1
        if min(counts) == 0:
            lost_model_total += 1
            if is_positive(phi):
                positive_without_model += 1
                lost_model_and_positive += 1
    print(f"  denotations of depth ≤ {depth} over {{a, ⊥, Tc}}: {len(pool)}")
    print("  distribution of (#models at v(a)=F, #models at v(a)=T):")
    for key in sorted(census, key=lambda k: -census[k]):
        print(f"      {key} : {census[key]}")
    print(f"  denotations losing a model for some valuation: {lost_model_total}")
    print(f"  ... of which positive: {positive_without_model}  (theory predicts 0)")
    assert positive_without_model == 0
    mixed = sum(1 for phi in pool
                if len({len(models({'c': phi}, {'a': b})) for b in (False, True)}) > 1)
    print(f"  denotations whose model count DEPENDS on the base valuation: {mixed}")
    print("  ⇒ every positive denotation is solvable for every valuation, and")
    print("    conservativity genuinely has to be stated per valuation.")


def demo_conservativity_audit() -> None:
    """Brute-force check that conservative tangles prove nothing new."""
    banner("8.  BRUTE-FORCE CONSERVATIVITY AUDIT")
    atoms = ["a", "b"]
    cases: List[Tuple[str, Tangle]] = [
        ("truth-teller  c ↦ Tc", {"c": Tr("c")}),
        ("two loops     p ↦ Tp, q ↦ Tq", {"p": Tr("p"), "q": Tr("q")}),
        ("mixed  q ↦ ⊥, p ↦ Tq → Tp", {"q": Fls(), "p": Imp(Tr("q"), Tr("p"))}),

        assert (bad == 0) == expandable_everywhere(den, atoms)

    print("    something new precisely when some valuation admits no model.")

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Atom:
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Fls:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Imp:
    left: object
    right: object


def show(f: object) -> str:
    if isinstance(f, Atom):
        return f.name
    if isinstance(f, Fls):
        return "⊥"
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return f"¬{show(f.left)}" if isinstance(f.right, Fls) else f"({show(f.left)} → {show(f.right)})"


def evaluate(f: object, v: Dict[str, bool]) -> bool:
    if isinstance(f, Atom):
        return v[f.name]
    if isinstance(f, Fls):
        return False
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return (not evaluate(f.left, v)) or evaluate(f.right, v)


def small_formulas(atoms: List[str]) -> List[object]:
    base: List[object] = [Fls()] + [Atom(a) for a in atoms]
    out = list(base)
    for p in base:
        for q in base:
            out.append(Imp(p, q))
    return list({show(f): f for f in out}.values())


def entails(theory: List[object], target: object, atoms: List[str],
            loop: Optional[Callable[[bool], bool]]) -> bool:
    """Entailment; `loop` is the loop equation right-hand side w ↦ den(c)(w)."""
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(atoms)):
        v = dict(zip(atoms, bits))
        witnesses = [w for w in (False, True) if w == loop(w)] if loop else [None]
        for _w in witnesses:
            if all(evaluate(f, v) for f in theory) and not evaluate(target, v):
                return False
    return True

    atoms = ["a", "b"]
    pool = small_formulas(atoms)
    tangles: List[Tuple[str, Optional[Callable[[bool], bool]]]] = [

        ("truth-teller  T c ↔ T c", lambda w: w),
        ("liar          T c ↔ ¬T c", lambda w: not w),
    ]
    print(f"pool of truth-free sentences: {len(pool)}  "
          f"({', '.join(show(f) for f in pool[:6])}, ...)")
    baseline: Dict[Tuple[str, str], bool] = {}
    for label, loop in tangles:
        yes = 0
        changed = 0
        for th in pool:
            for tg in pool:
                val = entails([th], tg, atoms, loop)
                yes += int(val)
                key = (show(th), show(tg))
                if loop is None:
                    baseline[key] = val
                elif val != baseline[key]:
                    changed += 1
        total = len(pool) ** 2
        note = "" if loop is None else f"   entailments changed vs. the old language: {changed}"
        print(f"{label:26s} entailing pairs: {yes:4d} / {total}{note}")
    print()
    print("The truth-teller changes 0 entailments: the strange loop is free.")
    print("The liar turns every pair into an entailment: its theory is inconsistent.")

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Tuple

Assignment = Dict[str, bool]
Sentence = Callable[[Dict[str, bool], Assignment], bool]  # (base valuation, names) -> truth


def revise(den: Dict[str, Sentence], v: Dict[str, bool], w: Assignment) -> Assignment:
    """One application of the revision operator R(w)(c) = value of den(c) at w."""
    return {c: den[c](v, w) for c in den}


def kleene(den: Dict[str, Sentence], v: Dict[str, bool], start: bool) -> Tuple[Assignment, int]:
    """Iterate the revision operator from the constant assignment `start`.

    For a positive tangle the operator is monotone on the powerset lattice of
    names, so the iteration is monotone and stabilises after at most |names|
    steps at the least fixed point (start=False) or the greatest (start=True).
    Returns the fixed point and the number of steps used.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    w: Assignment = {c: start for c in den}
    for step in range(len(den) + 1):
        w2 = revise(den, v, w)
        if w2 == w:
            return w, step
        w = w2
    return w, len(den) + 1


def is_determinate(den: Dict[str, Sentence], v: Dict[str, bool]) -> bool:
    """A positive tangle pins its truth predicate down iff lfp = gfp.

    Linear-time determinacy test: no enumeration of the 2^n assignments needed.
    """
    lfp, _ = kleene(den, v, False)
    gfp, _ = kleene(den, v, True)
    return lfp == gfp

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple

Edge = Tuple[str, str, int]  # (source name, target name, slack: 1 negative, 0 positive)


def relaxation_rank(names: List[str], edges: List[Edge]) -> Optional[Dict[str, int]]:
    """Least rank satisfying all constraints, or None if the system is infeasible."""
    rank: Dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in names}

def obstruction(names: List[str], edges: List[Edge]) -> Optional[List[str]]:

    for (src, tgt, _slack) in edges:
        successors[src].append(tgt)

    def reaches(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
        seen: Set[str] = set()
        stack = [a]
        while stack:
            x = stack.pop()
            if x == b:
                return True
            if x in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(x)
            stack.extend(successors[x])
        return False

    for (src, tgt, slack) in edges:
        if slack == 1 and reaches(tgt, src):
            return [src, tgt, src]  # a negative edge lying on a cycle

from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Atom:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Fls:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tr:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Imp:
    left: object
    right: object


def show(f: object) -> str:
    if isinstance(f, Atom):
        return "a"
    if isinstance(f, Fls):
        return "F"
    if isinstance(f, Tr):
        return "T"
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return f"({show(f.left)}>{show(f.right)})"


def evaluate(f: object, v: bool, w: bool) -> bool:
    if isinstance(f, Atom):
        return v
    if isinstance(f, Fls):
        return False
    if isinstance(f, Tr):
        return w
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return (not evaluate(f.left, v, w)) or evaluate(f.right, v, w)


def occurs_pol(f: object, positive: bool) -> bool:
    if isinstance(f, (Atom, Fls)):
        return False
    if isinstance(f, Tr):
        return positive
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return occurs_pol(f.left, not positive) or occurs_pol(f.right, positive)


def enumerate_formulas(depth: int) -> List[object]:
    out: List[object] = [Fls(), Atom(), Tr()]
    for _ in range(depth):
        new = [Imp(p, q) for p in out for q in out]
        out = list({show(f): f for f in out + new}.values())
    return out

    return tuple(sum(1 for w in (False, True) if w == evaluate(f, v, w))  # type: ignore[return-value]

/* ---------- parser ---------- */
function tokenize(s){
  const out=[]; let i=0;
  while(i<s.length){
    const c=s[i];
    if(/\s/.test(c)){i++;continue;}
    if(s.startsWith("->",i)){out.push("->");i+=2;continue;}
    if("()~&|".includes(c)){out.push(c);i++;continue;}
    if(c==='T'&&"pqr".includes(s[i+1])){out.push("T"+s[i+1]);i+=2;continue;}
    if(c==='a'){out.push("a");i++;continue;}
    if(c==='F'){out.push("F");i++;continue;}
    throw new Error("unexpected character '"+c+"'");
  }
  return out;
}
function parse(str){
  const t=tokenize(str); let k=0;
  function peek(){return t[k];}
  function eat(x){if(t[k]!==x)throw new Error("expected "+x);k++;}
  function atomP(){
    const x=peek();
    if(x==='('){eat('(');const e=impP();eat(')');return e;}
    if(x==='~'){eat('~');return {t:'imp',l:atomP(),r:{t:'fls'}};}
    if(x==='a'){k++;return {t:'atom'};}
    if(x==='F'){k++;return {t:'fls'};}
    if(x&&x[0]==='T'){k++;return {t:'tr',n:x[1]};}
    throw new Error("unexpected end of formula");
  }
  function andP(){let e=atomP();while(peek()==='&'){eat('&');e={t:'and',l:e,r:atomP()};}return e;}
  function orP(){let e=andP();while(peek()==='|'){eat('|');e={t:'or',l:e,r:andP()};}return e;}
  function impP(){const e=orP();if(peek()==='->'){eat('->');return {t:'imp',l:e,r:impP()};}return e;}
  const e=impP(); if(k!==t.length) throw new Error("trailing input"); return e;
}
/* ---------- semantics ---------- */
function evalF(f,v,w){
  switch(f.t){
    case 'atom':return v;
    case 'fls':return false;
    case 'tr':return !!w[f.n];
    case 'and':return evalF(f.l,v,w)&&evalF(f.r,v,w);
    case 'or':return evalF(f.l,v,w)||evalF(f.r,v,w);
    case 'imp':return (!evalF(f.l,v,w))||evalF(f.r,v,w);
  }
}
function occPol(f,c,pos){
  switch(f.t){
    case 'atom': case 'fls': return false;
    case 'tr': return pos && f.n===c;
    case 'and': case 'or': return occPol(f.l,c,pos)||occPol(f.r,c,pos);
    case 'imp': return occPol(f.l,c,!pos)||occPol(f.r,c,pos);
  }
}
function occurs(f,c){return occPol(f,c,true)||occPol(f,c,false);}
function show(f){
  switch(f.t){
    case 'atom':return 'a'; case 'fls':return '⊥'; case 'tr':return 'T'+f.n;
    case 'and':return '('+show(f.l)+' ∧ '+show(f.r)+')';
    case 'or':return '('+show(f.l)+' ∨ '+show(f.r)+')';
    case 'imp':return f.r.t==='fls'?('¬'+show(f.l)):('('+show(f.l)+' → '+show(f.r)+')');
  }
}

function assignments(names){
  const out=[];const n=names.length;
  for(let m=0;m<(1<<n);m++){const w={};names.forEach((c,i)=>w[c]=!!(m&(1<<i)));out.push(w);}
  return out;
}
function isModel(den,names,v,w){return names.every(c=>w[c]===evalF(den[c],v,w));}
function revise(den,names,v,w){const o={};names.forEach(c=>o[c]=evalF(den[c],v,w));return o;}
function fixpoint(den,names,v,start){
  let w={};names.forEach(c=>w[c]=start);

    const w2=revise(den,names,v,w);
    if(names.every(c=>w2[c]===w[c]))return w;
    w=w2;
  }
  return w;
}
function isPositive(den,names){return names.every(c=>names.every(d=>!occPol(den[c],d,false)));}
function rankSolve(den,names,strictAll){
  const rk={};names.forEach(c=>rk[c]=0);

  }
  return null;
}

  html+='<span class="badge '+(grd?'yes':'no')+'">grounded: '+(grd?'yes, rank '+JSON.stringify(grd):'no')+'</span>';
  html+='<span class="badge '+(loc?'yes':'no')+'">locally stratified: '+(loc?'yes, rank '+JSON.stringify(loc):'no')+'</span>';
  html+='</div>';
  document.getElementById('diag').innerHTML=html;

  let tabs='';let allSolvable=true;let counts=[];
  [false,true].forEach(v=>{

    counts.push(ms.length); if(ms.length===0) allSolvable=false;
    const lfp=pos?fixpoint(den,names,v,false):null;

    tabs+='<h3 style="font-size:15px;margin:14px 0 6px">base valuation a = '+(v?'true':'false')+

    tabs+='<table><tr>'+names.map(c=>'<th>T'+c+'</th>').join('')+
          names.map(c=>'<th>⟦den('+c+')⟧</th>').join('')+'<th>model?</th><th></th></tr>';
    assignments(names).forEach(w=>{
      const vals=names.map(c=>evalF(den[c],v,w));

      let tag='';

                   else if(names.every(c=>w[c]===gfp[c]))tag='credulous (greatest)'; }
      tabs+='<tr style="'+(ok?'background:#16351f':'')+'">'+
            names.map(c=>'<td>'+(w[c]?'T':'F')+'</td>').join('')+
            vals.map(x=>'<td>'+(x?'T':'F')+'</td>').join('')+

      'so this tangle adds no truth-free consequence to any truth-free theory.</div>';
